Create a visual representation of a landscape with three hills. Each hill is drawn as a quadratic Bezier curve, forming a smooth, rounded shape. The hills are positioned horizontally across the SVG canvas, with varying sizes and positions. The visual includes a title centered at the top, describing the scene as "D3 Quadratic Bezier Hills."

The code is written in TypeScript and runs in a web browser environment. The rendering target is an SVG element within the HTML document's body.

The input data consists of an array of objects, each representing a hill with properties such as bottom-left corner coordinates, width, height, a control point for the quadratic Bezier curve, stroke color, and stroke width. There is no data fetching or parsing from external sources; the data is hardcoded within the script. The control point for each hill is calculated using a quadratic Bezier control point function based on the hill's dimensions and position.

The background of the SVG canvas is a sky blue color, providing a backdrop for the hills. Each hill has a gradient fill transitioning from a lighter orange at the top to a darker orange at the bottom, giving a sense of depth and dimension. The hills have a brown stroke outlining their shape, adding definition. The title text is centered at the top of the canvas, styled with a sans-serif font, medium size, and dark gray color, ensuring readability against the blue background. There is no animation or interactivity in the visual.

Create a line chart that visualizes multiple data series over a common x-axis labeled "Cycle" and a y-axis labeled "Value". Each series is represented by a line connecting data points, with a legend positioned to the right of the chart identifying each series by color. The chart is titled "Trace.js Simulation Analysis".

The language used is TypeScript, and the runtime environment is a web browser. The rendering target is an HTML element, specifically a div, which is used to display a chart.

The inputs consist of an array of objects, each representing a data series with an identifier, a set of numerical values, a color for the line, and a flag indicating whether to show the line. The data is transformed into a format suitable for charting by extracting the series identifiers and their corresponding values into an array of arrays. Additionally, a mapping of series identifiers to their respective colors is created for styling purposes.

The chart is 600 pixels wide and 400 pixels high, with a right padding of 40 pixels to accommodate the legend. The lines are colored distinctly for each series: red, green, and blue. Data points are marked on the lines, enhancing visibility. The x-axis and y-axis are labeled, and the legend is interactive, allowing users to identify series by color. The layout is clean and minimalistic, focusing on the data representation.

Create a bar chart with vertical bars representing the data values. Each bar's height is proportional to its corresponding data value. The bars are arranged horizontally in a row. Above each bar, a text label displays the numerical value of the data it represents. A title is positioned at the top center of the chart, indicating the chart's purpose.

The code is written in TypeScript and runs in a web browser environment. The rendering target is an SVG element within the Document Object Model (DOM).

The input data is a static array of numbers: [10, 15, 20, 25, 30]. This array represents the values to be visualized in the bar chart. Each number corresponds to the height of a bar in the chart. The data is directly used without any additional fetching or complex transformations.

The chart is contained within a bordered rectangular SVG area. Each bar is colored in a uniform steel blue shade and has a consistent width with small gaps between them. The bars are aligned along the bottom of the SVG container. The text labels above the bars are centered horizontally and use a sans-serif font in black color. The font size of the labels is smaller than the title, which is bold and centrally aligned at the top of the SVG area. The overall layout is clean and straightforward, with no animations or interactivity.

Create a horizontal bar chart displaying study counts for different members. The chart includes labeled axes, with the horizontal axis representing the study count and the vertical axis listing the members. Each bar's length corresponds to the study count value for a member, visually comparing the values across different members.

The language used is TypeScript, and the runtime environment is a web browser. The rendering target is an SVG element within the DOM.

The inputs consist of a configuration object defining dimensions, margins, bar color, and labels, along with a mock data array containing objects with 'member' and 'studyCount' properties. The data is directly embedded in the code and does not involve any fetching or external parsing. The data is used to determine the scales and dimensions of the visual elements, with transformations applied to map data values to visual positions and sizes.

The visual features a clean and simple layout with a small margin around the chart. The bars are horizontally oriented and colored in a light purple shade. The chart includes a title labeled "Age" above it. The horizontal axis is labeled "Study Count" and includes tick marks for reference. The vertical axis lists the member labels alongside each corresponding bar. The overall style is minimalistic, with a sans-serif font used for text elements, and there is no animation or interactivity involved.

Create a line chart with two data series plotted on a two-dimensional plane. Each series is represented by a line connecting data points, with one series appearing above the other. The chart includes labeled axes, with the horizontal axis labeled as 'X Axis' and the vertical axis labeled as 'Y Axis'. A title, 'Sample Line Chart', is displayed to describe the chart's purpose.

The language used is TypeScript, and the runtime environment is a web browser. The rendering target is the Document Object Model (DOM), specifically within an HTML container element.

The input data consists of two arrays of numerical values, each associated with a label ('data1' and 'data2'). These arrays are structured as columns, representing two separate data series to be plotted on the chart. There is no data fetching or parsing involved, as the data is hardcoded within the script. The data is directly used to generate the visual without any transformations or state updates.

The appearance consists of two distinct lines, each in a different color, representing the data series. The lines are thin and connect circular data points plotted along the axes. The layout positions the legend on the right side of the chart, providing a key for the data series. The chart title is prominently displayed, and the axes labels are oriented parallel to their respective axes. There is no animation or interactivity described in the visual.

Create a visual representation of a simplified map projection of the United States, focusing on the states of California and Nevada. The map is displayed in an SVG container, with each state rendered as a polygon. The state names are labeled on the map, positioned at the centroid of each state's polygon. A title is placed at the top of the map to describe the visual as a minimal US map projection example.

The language used is TypeScript, and the runtime environment is a web browser. The rendering target is an SVG element within the Document Object Model (DOM).

The input data consists of a minimal mock GeoJSON object representing two US states: California and Nevada. Each state is described as a feature with properties for the state name and geometry defined as a polygon with specified coordinates. The data is directly embedded in the code and does not involve any external fetching or parsing. The coordinates are transformed using a geo-albers-usa projection to fit within the specified viewbox dimensions.

The appearance includes a light gray background for the SVG container and a teal fill color for the state polygons. The state borders are outlined with a thin black stroke. State names are displayed in black, centered within each state polygon, using a sans-serif font. The title is bold and centered at the top of the SVG, with a larger font size than the state labels. The layout is static, with no animations or interactivity implemented in the visual.

Create a bar chart that visually represents the data. Each bar corresponds to a data entry, with the height of the bar proportional to its value. The chart includes axes with labels, a title at the top, and numerical labels above each bar indicating the exact value.

The code is written in TypeScript and runs in a web browser environment. The rendering target is an SVG element within the Document Object Model (DOM).

The input data is a static array of objects, each containing a 'name' and a 'value' property. The data represents categorical names associated with numerical values. The data is directly used to create scales and render graphical elements, with no additional fetching or parsing. Transformations include mapping data to scales for positioning and sizing the visual elements.

The chart is laid out with a series of vertical bars aligned horizontally. The bars are uniformly colored in a shade of blue. The chart includes a title at the top in bold, larger font, and axis labels in a smaller font. The x-axis labels are positioned below the bars, while the y-axis labels are to the left of the chart. Each bar has a numerical label above it, centered horizontally, in a smaller, dark font. The overall layout is clean, with a focus on readability and simplicity. There are no animations or interactive elements.

Create a line chart with two distinct lines representing different data sets. The chart includes labeled axes, with the x-axis labeled as "X Axis" and the y-axis labeled as "Y Axis". A title "Sample Line Chart" is displayed above the chart. A legend is positioned to the right of the chart to differentiate between the two data lines.

The language used is TypeScript, and the runtime environment is a web browser. The rendering target is the Document Object Model (DOM).

The input data consists of two sets of numerical values, each associated with a label ('data1' and 'data2'). These data sets are structured in columns and are used to generate two lines on the chart. There is no data fetching or parsing involved, as the data is hardcoded within the script. The data is transformed into a visual representation as a line chart.

The chart is laid out with a clear and simple design, featuring two lines plotted on a grid. Each line is represented in a different color for distinction. The x-axis and y-axis are labeled, and tick marks are present to indicate data points. The legend on the right provides a key for interpreting the lines. The chart title is prominently displayed at the top. The chart is static, with no animations or interactivity.
